To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nebulizer is an effective method of delivering a radioactive tracer to the lungs of cats, and the deposition of the radioactive tracer can be quantified with a gamma camera.
the nebulized aerosol of a radiopharmaceutical was deposited primarily in the airways of awake cats and that the radiopharmaceutical could be detected by SPECT imaging.

the development of a novel, nebulized radiotracer for the assessment of regional ventilation and perfusion in the lungs.
the development of a radiopharmaceutical for the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism.
the development of a radiopharmaceutical for the imaging of pulmonary emboli in cats.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method for measuring pulmonary deposition of a radiopharmaceutical nebulized into awake cats.
we have demonstrated that the pulmonary deposition and retention of a nebulizer-delivered radiopharmaceutical can be quantified in an animal model using SPECT.
the nebulized radiotracer is not distributed uniformly within the lungs of awake cats, but that the radiotracer deposition pattern is similar in the lungs of awake and anesthetized cats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pulmonary deposition of a radiopharmaceutical aerosol in awake cats can be accurately measured with a gamma camera.
there is a lot of variation in the amount of radiation that a cat receives from a single dose of a radioactive drug.
the nebulized aerosol of a 99mTc-DTPA agent can be deposited throughout the lungs in awake cats, and that the deposition is dependent on the respiratory pattern of the animal.
